Julian Tinoco is the creator of OLA.
OLA allows users to automatically identify display discrepancies between browsers and validate the responsiveness of websites.
The project was launched on Kickstarter with a funding goal of $6,002.
The funding period for OLA was from May 24, 2019, to June 23, 2019.

fact_previews: OLA (Online Layout Analyzer) is a cross-browser testing tool developed by Julian Tinoco.
OLA breaks websites into a tree of nodes and analyzes them from the perspective of different platforms.
OLA compares platforms to ensure that websites are fully responsive.
Reports generated by OLA offer side-by-side comparisons to view the entire website at a glance.
Manual testing of all platforms can take weeks and is prone to error.

fact_previews: Web Designers spend about 30%-40% of their time checking the responsiveness of their websites.
OLA was created to address the time Web Designers spend on checking website responsiveness.
Lacetech's team is growing and is located in different countries, including Canada, Australia, and Colombia.
A normal website with 10 pages, 10 different resolutions, and two browsers can provide a report in less than 5 minutes when using OLA.
Lacetech works with the version of the software for 6 months to assure its stability before launching the code for the public.
